deal._note: Round repriced 2026-08-04: R8.0m for 15%. Pre/post are exact (8 / 0.15 = 53,333,333). The price is justified by the plan itself — four revenue rungs plus territory sponsorship — not by an external valuation opinion. The independent DCF was removed 2026-08-04: it is out of date and must not be reinstated without a fresh one.

monthlyRevenueZAR._note: historical endpoints (Jul–Dec 2025), chart retired from public page

modelForecast._source: GetLucky_Valuation_Model.xlsx — Valuation tab annual roll-up (supersedes the 2025 deck forecast)
modelForecast._streams: Revenue is built from four reported streams, all core to the plan: coursesAndApp (installed courses, membership and the global app subscription, including the contracted Santam sponsorship), simulators, territorySponsorship (the Santam deal repeated per market) and inPlayUpsells (the add-on menu, which attaches to attempts already in the model and never creates new volume). revenueZAR is the total. Report as composition.
modelForecast._costBase: Cost base raised 2026-08-04 on user instruction — "increase the expenses & budgets to make sure we get the revenue". Base opex R350k -> R450k/month and ops scaling 0.65 -> 0.68, plus lower per-stream EBITDA margins to fund delivery: simulators 50% -> 42% (integration engineering and operator marketing support), territory sponsorship 60% -> 52% (local activation and partner servicing), upsells 65% -> 60% (product build and payment costs). Annual opex roughly doubles by 2029. Revenue and the valuation milestones are UNCHANGED — the milestones are struck off revenue multiples, so a heavier cost base does not move them or the investor IRR; it makes the plan deliverable, not smaller.

simulatorChannel._note: A core revenue stream in the plan, not optional upside. Launches 2027 once the integration this round funds is built. Ramp and sensitivity are modelled in the Simulator tab of the pro forma workbook.
simulatorChannel.status: Launching 2027 — integration funded by this round

revenueSplitPct._note: Operator takes 30% — more than a course's 10% because the operator brings the venues, the software and the distribution, and Get Lucky installs no hardware. Insurance premium held at 24%, matching the on-course model.

simulatorChannel._volumeBasis: Attach rate applied to ~94M annual simulator rounds in South Korea alone (research.json: korea-sim-rounds) — Golfzon's home network. Golfzon's non-Korea venues and every other operator on targetOperators are excluded from the model.
simulatorChannel.agreementStatus: No operator agreement is signed as at August 2026. State this once, plainly, in the dataroom assumptions and the simulator document risk section — do not repeat it as a badge or a caveat on every figure.
simulatorChannel.route: Ernie Els holds direct relationships with the target operators and opens the door himself.

sensitivity2029._note: Adoption range around the plan, with every other stream held at plan. Upsell revenue moves with simulator volume, so it is recomputed per row rather than held flat.

territorySponsorship._note: Sponsorship is a proven, repeatable line, not a projection: Santam signed R9m over three years (R2.5m -> R3.0m -> R3.5m) to be attached to this product in South Africa, a ~150k-golfer market. Each target territory repeats that deal with an anchor insurer partner brand, phased by market-entry year. South African sponsorship already sits inside the coursesAndApp stream; this block is the additional territories only.
territorySponsorship._sizing: New-territory deals are set below the SA run-rate at entry and grow with the installed base. They are NOT scaled linearly off golfer counts — sponsorship is negotiated and lumpy, and a linear scale off a 25M-golfer market would produce figures no sponsor would sign. Every figure here is a live input on the Sponsorship tab.

inPlayUpsells._note: The add-on menu sold at the moment of maximum intent — after a golfer has paid and is standing over the ball. Upsells attach to attempts ALREADY in the model (subscriber rounds and simulator challenges); they never create new volume, so there is no double-count with the other streams. Launches 2027 with the app build this round funds.
inPlayUpsells.status: Launching 2027 — built with the app, funded by this round

menu.name: Jackpot upgrade
menu.detail: Trade up mid-round: $100 buys a shot at a $100,000 insured prize instead of the standard pot.

menu.name: Double up
menu.detail: Doubles your prize if you ace it. Cheapest yes on the menu and the highest attach.

menu.name: Three for two
menu.detail: Three swings for the price of two. Raises attempts per visit without touching the prize.

menu.name: Nearest the pin
menu.detail: A guaranteed prize if you finish inside three feet. Monetises the 12,499 attempts out of 12,500 that are not an ace — the single biggest lever on perceived value.

menu.name: The highlight reel
menu.detail: The produced clip of your shot, scored and branded, ready to post. No insurance component — pure margin, and every share is marketing.

menu.name: The group pot
menu.detail: A fourball buys in, closest to the pin takes the pot, Get Lucky takes a fee. Turns a solo purchase into four.

assumptions._note: Attach rates are set against the price point of the underlying entry: a golfer paying ~R200 a swing is a very different buyer to one paying $1 in a simulator, so the two are modelled separately.
assumptions.coreBasis: Subscriber rounds — subscribers x 4 rounds/month x 12
assumptions.simBasis: Simulator challenges from the simulator ramp

valuationModel.comps: Strava / Peloton / Whoop engaged-community businesses trade 5–10× revenue
